title: ר' ישמעאל בר יוסי

paragraphs: (a) He is the son of R. Yose ben Ḥalafta (Avot, chapter 4). The author of Halikhot Olam erred in writing that he was the son of R. Yose HaGelili, as in chapter Kol Kitvei; see there (118b). So writes Yuḥasin in Seder HaDorot. Yet he himself erred under R. Yose HaGelili in listing his sons as R. Yishmael son of R. Yose HaGelili and R. Ḥanina son of R. Yose HaGelili, forgetting what he wrote here about Halikhot Olam's error.

(b) Rabbi's beloved colleague. He had four brothers (see above, R. Yose). The king appointed him to seize thieves and bandits. Elijah encountered him and said, 'How long will you hand over our God's people to be killed?' He answered, 'What can I do? It is the king's command.' He said, 'Your father fled to Asia; you flee to Laodicea,' chapter HaPo'alim (84a). This requires examination, for his father R. Yose fled to Tzippori; see what I wrote there. When he and R. Eliezer son of R. Shimon stood face to face, a pair of oxen could pass beneath their bellies between them. His member was like a nine-kav [vessel]; see Tosafot there. Rabbenu Barukh explains 'his member' as the measure of his arm, as in the first chapter of Berakhot, 'He uncovered his member and light fell'; he does not read 'his arm' [דרעיה]. He was a heavy man and therefore was late entering the study house [התאחד, provisional reading]. He stepped over [the seated people] as he went. Avdan said, 'Who is this stepping over the heads of the holy people?' He answered, 'It is I, who have come to learn Torah from Rabbi.' He said, 'Are you fit to learn from Rabbi?' He replied, 'Was Moses fit to learn from the Almighty?' He said, 'Are you Moses?' He answered, 'Is your teacher God?' Rav Yosef said: Rabbi received his recompense in this world, for he said 'your teacher' rather than 'my teacher.' (That is, Rabbi received his due for hearing and not protesting—Rashi. Arukh explains: judgment was exacted from him; some say he received his portion and lot of punishment corresponding to his liability.) Meanwhile a yevamah came for ḥalitzah. Rabbi told Avdan, 'Go examine her.' He went. R. Yishmael said to him: Father said thus: 'man' is written, but a woman may be either minor or adult. Rabbi told Avdan, 'Stay in your place; an elder has already ruled.' Avdan came stepping over [people]. R. Yishmael said, 'One whom the holy people need may step over their heads; one whom they do not need should not.' Rabbi told Avdan, 'Stand where you are.' At that moment Avdan developed tzara'at, his two sons drowned, and his two daughters-in-law refused their marriages. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said, 'Blessed is the Merciful One, who shamed Avdan in this world,' chapter Mitzvat Ḥalitzah (105b). In my opinion the law does not follow R. Yishmael, as in the Mishnah at the beginning of chapter Ba Siman (48a); Tosafot there writes likewise. He instructed Rabbi in three matters, Arvei Pesaḥim (112b). On folio 118b, when he fell ill, Rabbi sent him: 'Tell us several things in your father's name.' Rashbam writes: in several places we find Rabbi sending to him during his illness; perhaps he suffered many illnesses. In the first chapter of Shabbat (15a), when he fell ill they sent to him: “Rabbi,” [and asked him to repeat teachings in his father’s name]. In a separate report he said, “I can write out all Scripture from memory,” Jerusalem Talmud, Megillah, chapter 4, halakhah 1. He is a tanna and may disagree, chapter Bammeh Ishah (64b). He visited R. Shimon son of R. Yose ben Lakonya's house. They gave him a cup, and he drank it at once. They said, 'Does the master not accept that one who drinks his cup all at once is a glutton?' He answered, 'They did not say so in the case of your small cup, your sweet wine, and my broad belly,' Pesaḥim (86b). A man was carrying a bundle and said to R. Yishmael, 'Lift it for me'; he gave him its value, beyond the letter of the law, Bava Metzia (30b). He interpreted dreams (see above, R. Yishmael, R. Akiva's colleague). At the end of chapter 2 of Niddah (20, end of side b), 'R. Yishmael son of R. Yosef' should read Yose; in the new Shas, ל״ח [probably 'not corrected,' uncertain abbreviation]. In Jerusalem Talmud, Yevamot, chapter 7, halakhah 2: 'R. Yishmael son of R. Yose in Abaye's name' should read 'son of R. Yose in his father's name'; afterward it brings R. Yishmael son of R. Yose.

(c) In R. Abba's name, Midrash Ḥazit, at 'With me from Lebanon'—this requires examination. R. Elazar HaKappar. R. Bisa, or Bisna. Rav Huna, in his name. He spoke to R. Ḥiyya the Babylonian. R. Ḥama bar Bisna asked him. In Jerusalem Talmud, Ketubbot, chapter 5, halakhah 10: son of R. Yasi. R. Ḥanina spoke in his name. In Babylonian Shabbat (49, end of side a), R. Ḥanina said, 'Thus said R. Yishmael son of R. Yose'; Kiddushin (71). He said to him, 'Here Father prayed the Shabbat prayer on Friday,' Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 10. He cursed R. Ḥanina with croup for splitting [a lump of earth for the comparison], etc., Niddah (20, end of side a). Rabbi asked him, Shabbat (113b, 119a). He spoke to R. Yehudah son of R. Ilai. He saw R. Yishmael ben Elisha. Rav Kahana, in his name, Arvei Pesaḥim (119a). He heard in R. Matya ben Ḥarash's name, Yoma (84a). In R. Natan Tosfa'ah's name, Ohalot, chapter 5. R. Anani bar Sasson, in his name. R. Pinḥas ben Yair. R. Shemuel, in his name. He visited R. Shimon son of R. Yose ben Lakonya's house (see above). R. Shimon son of Rabbi, in his name, Zevaḥim (59a).
